subject: Ops Handoff: Telemetry setup, alert flow, and runbook ownership
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finlogic.com>
Cc: support@finlogic.com
Date: Fri, 2 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ops Handoff: Telemetry setup, alert flow, and runbook ownership

Hi team,

This thread is to kickoff the CS -> Ops/Platform handoff for FinLogic's observability implementation. Alex, thanks again for the quick demo last week — this thread will capture owners, deliverables, and a proposed timeline so we can align before the production rollout.

High-level goals:
- Confirm dashboards and SLO targets for the primary inference endpoints (text-generation and embeddings)
- Install tracing hooks and agree on sampling strategy
- Finalize error taxonomy and alert routing (pager/Slack/escalation)
- Deliver a first-pass runbook for on-call and incident triage

Initial asks for FinLogic (Alex):
1) Link to any existing dashboards or instrumentation runbooks you have (Datadog/Grafana links are fine)
2) Expected peak qps and typical sequence lengths (so we can size batching/latency SLOs)
3) Contact for IAM/credentials to access test telemetry (read-only)

Proposed owners (subject to confirmation):
- Dashboards & SLOs: Marissa Cole
- Tracing & SDK hooks: Aditya Rao
- Alert routing & runbooks: Diego Fernandez

I attached a starter runbook (runbook-v1.md) and a short alert matrix from FinLogic they shared; Diego/Marissa/Aditya, can you reply with availability for a 60-minute kickoff next week and any pre-kickoff requests you have?

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: runbook-v1.md, finlogic-alert-matrix.xlsx
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sat, 3 Jun 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops Handoff: Telemetry setup, alert flow, and runbook ownership

Thanks, Olga — looping in initial notes.

Quick answers / questions:
- Availability: I'm free Tue 6/7 10:00–12:00 PT or Thu 6/9 14:00–16:00 PT for a 60-minute kickoff.
- Pre-kickoff ask: a read-only view into FinLogic's Datadog org (service: finlogic-inference) would speed up scoping.

Notes on alert routing: we should aim to avoid noisy token-level alerts. Suggested first-pass alerts (we can refine in kickoff):
- P50/P95 latency breach for text-generation endpoints (alert to platform on-call)
- Error rate spike > 0.5% over rolling 5m (alert to CS + engineering)
- KV cache pressure / OOM signals (urgent, page infra on-call)

Aditya — can you prepare a short tracing hook snippet for the client SDK? I want to review sampling and tag conventions before we push into test.

Alex — if you can drop typical qps and avg seq lengths, we'll sketch SLOs ahead of the meeting.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Platform Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none

Hi all — thanks for the quick follow-ups.

Availability: Thu 6/9 14:00 PT works best for us (we can stretch to 15:00 if needed).

Quick background and artifacts:
- Datadog link (read-only): https://app.datadoghq.com/finlogic/inference (we'll invite redwoodops@finlogic to the org)
- Typical production profile: 180 qps peak across two primary routes; avg seq length ~128 tokens; spikes up to 1k qps during promos
- SLO targets we want to aim for initially: 99.5% p99 < 800ms for text-generation; 99% p99 < 300ms for embeddings

I've attached our internal alert matrix and a current escalation list. Also FYI: security will send a short questionnaire this week (SOC2 scoping) — Olga, can you confirm who handles item-level evidence requests?

Slack channel for telemetry threads: #finlogic-telemetry (we've invited olga.petrov and diego.fernandez)

Alex
